results: Memory, outer cap (original#43): with ECOSYSTEM_JOB_MEMORY_MAX=300M the job ended with exit=137 and bash reported `ecosystem-bounded-run: line 64: ... Killed /usr/bin/systemd-run --user --scope ... --property=MemoryMax=$job_max ... --property=OOMPolicy=kill`. Neither ALLOCATED_ALL nor MEMORYERROR was printed. The kill is consistent with the MemoryMax OOM policy; no OOM event log was captured.

Fork, outer TasksMax=20 (original#45): `apply-seccomp: fork(worker): Resource temporarily unavailable`, exit=1, and the Python loop printed nothing. The limit was hit while srt itself was starting (its apply-seccomp helper could not fork), before the workload ran, so this shows the outer cap binds srt startup; it does not show the cap stopping the workload's own fork loop.

CPU, outer RuntimeMaxSec=5 (original#47): `exit=0 elapsed=6s`, and LOOP_COMPLETED was not printed, so the 30 s loop was cut short at about the runtime limit; the wrapper sets no CPUQuota, so CPU-rate throttling was not exercised.
Disk (original#45): 50 MB dd inside srt succeeded (`52428800 bytes ... copied`, dd_exit=0) with 826G free; no quota existed to hit.

Source search (fix#51, fix#52): `find ...sandbox-runtime-0.0.77 -iname "*.js" | xargs grep -liE "rlimit|setrlimit|memory.*limit|RLIMIT"` printed nothing; `find ... -iname "*.js" | wc -l` printed 188; `grep -rliE "cgroup|memory.max|pids.max"` over the whole tree matched only node_modules/node-forge/lib/aesCipherSuites.js. The first search covered .js files only, so the native apply-seccomp helper and other non-JS files were not searched for rlimit/setrlimit.
note: sandbox-runtime 0.0.77 applied no memory or fork limit to small workloads (150 MB, 80 forks) and its JavaScript contains no rlimit/cgroup code by keyword search. The outer ecosystem-bounded-run scope stopped a memory hog (exit 137) and a CPU loop (runtime limit); the TasksMax=20 case failed during srt startup, so it does not show the workload being stopped. Remaining: disk-fill against a real quota, CPU-rate limiting, a fork case with a TasksMax large enough for srt to start, the native helper binaries, and VM-boundary or hostile-workload probes.
limits: ecosystem-bounded-run does not set CPUQuota, so CPU-rate limiting was not exercised at all (only wall-clock RuntimeMaxSec).

VM-boundary / hostile-workload testing beyond memory/fork/CPU/disk was not attempted (e.g. no syscall-fuzzing or privilege-escalation probes).
The fork-limit claim is weaker than previously stated: the TasksMax=20 run never reached the workload.
